claim: Lumos released runtime governance for Claude Code and Codex that observes and can block individual MCP and other tool calls before execution.
verifiedFacts: Lumos released MCP Governance for Claude Code and Codex.
The product records MCP/tool usage and can apply allow-or-deny policy before a tool call executes.
Lumos says coverage extends beyond MCP to Bash commands, file edits, browser use and locally added MCP servers.
Its product page says recorded call metadata includes human identity and policy decision.
inference: The Seed Loom authority thesis should distinguish evidence of authority from independent runtime enforcement at the exact action boundary.

Consultancy implication: a governed-agent review can compare declared scope with observed tool-call scope and identify over-broad inherited human permissions. Project disposition: Seed Loom CORE; Agent Runtime PRODUCTIZE only where enforcement is required.
significance: Very high: this is a direct market implementation of the evidence-versus-enforcement boundary Seed Loom has been trying to articulate.
assumptions: Lumos's released product behaves as its technical documentation describes.
knownLimitations: Latency, false-block rates and independent production outcomes are vendor reported or unavailable.
Runtime enforcement remains an external system capability, not evidence that Seed Loom should implement it.
